table.attribution: Janus FAERS time-to-onset table for the PIPC prescribing cascades, CC BY 4.0. PIPC columns: Rochon PA et al., Potentially inappropriate prescribing cascades (PIPC) list, Eur Geriatr Med 2025;16(5):1573-1584, doi:10.1007/s41999-025-01215-x, Table 1 (CC BY 4.0). Counts and intervals derived from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System quarterly data files (CC0 1.0); not an FDA endorsement.

caveats.class_membership: Drug A's class is matched on the ingredient-level ATC codes of each ingredient key with the cascade engine's matcher. This build uses the FAERS route field: suspect lines given by a local route (skin, eye, ear, nose, airways, vagina or uterus, mouth, joints, bladder) are not counted, except eye drops for row 3, rectal laxatives for row 47, nasal and inhaled forms of opioids, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines and dopaminergic medicines, and joint or lesion injections of systemic corticosteroids; lines without a route count. Exposure through the placenta or breast milk is never counted. Some keys are left out per class (excluded_class_keys, with reasons in data/onset_key_exclusions.csv); members_with_reports shows which keys drive a row.
caveats.clusters: Several distinct cases sometimes share the exact same therapy start and event dates: possible duplicate patients, a case series, or a literature or litigation batch. Each row gives largest_date_cluster and reports_in_clusters_ge3; when one identical date pair holds more than 25% of a row's reports the row publishes counts only (status cluster_dominated).
caveats.day_one: Dates on the 1st of a month are far more common in FAERS than chance (a month- or year-only date filled in with day 01), and a 1 January date can be off by most of a year. Each row gives day_one_reports and jan_one_reports and, as a sensitivity check, median_days_without_day_one; that check also drops genuine day-01 dates, so it is not a correction.
caveats.descriptive: Descriptive only. A time to onset here is the interval between a therapy start date and the event date that a reporter wrote down; it is not a causal estimate, it does not show that the medicine caused the event and it is not onset measured in people.
caveats.event_date_report_level: FAERS gives one event date per report, not per event term. In reports with several terms (multi_event_reports) the date may belong to another event than this row's.
caveats.median_interval: Use the exact order-statistic interval of the median (median_exact_ci_*). The percentile bootstrap interval is kept for comparison with the time machine and can understate the uncertainty on tied or small data (median_ci_degenerate marks a zero-width one).
caveats.not_incidence: FAERS is spontaneous reporting: not incidence and no denominator of exposed patients. Case versions are collapsed to the latest one, but duplicate cases sent by different reporters are not merged, so one patient can appear under several case ids. Counts are reports, never people.
caveats.receipt_window: The window is four quarters of reports by date received; event dates can be years earlier (see event_year_min and event_year_max). Old or rarely used medicines can have few or no reports in the window.
caveats.selection: Only reports with both a complete therapy start date and a complete event date carry an interval. That subset may not be representative of all reports (date completeness may differ by reporter type and by seriousness), and long-standing therapy is less often dated. candidates_without_interval_by_reason shows why the others have no interval.
caveats.shared_rows: PIPC rows that share drug A's class and the event key (they differ in drug B) have the same numbers; shared_with_positions names them.
caveats.shortest_interval: Per report the interval is taken from the most recently started class-member suspect line; after a switch within the class this is shorter than the time since the class was first started (median_days_earliest_class_start gives the other reading).
caveats.small_sample: Rows with fewer than 10 reports with an interval publish counts only; rows with 10-29 are flagged small_sample and their estimates are unstable; the intervals may understate the uncertainty.
caveats.weibull: The Weibull shape class reflects reporting artefacts (zero-day and day-01 heaping, the receipt window that cuts off late onsets) as much as timing; it is not a mechanism. It is published only for rows with at least 30 reports, at most 50% same-day intervals and at least 5 distinct intervals.
caveats.zero_day: A same-day interval (0 days) often means the reporter gave one date for both fields rather than a genuine same-day onset; heaping at zero pulls the median down. The zero-day count is published with every row. When more than half the intervals are 0 days (median_reflects_zero_heaping), the median and both intervals are 0 and show same-day heaping, not timing.

table.meddra_notice: Event terms are MedDRA Preferred Terms as published in FAERS. MedDRA® the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities terminology is the international medical terminology developed under the auspices of ICH. MedDRA® trademark is registered by IFPMA on behalf of ICH.

method.interval: per report, the interval from the most recently started class-member suspect line: the earliest complete THER.start_dt of that line to DEMO.event_dt, 0 to 3650 days
method.median: empirical median; quartiles by linear interpolation between order statistics (interpolated at small n)
method.median_interval_bootstrap: 95 % percentile bootstrap interval of the median, 1000 resamples, Python 3.12 random.Random seeded from (seed 20261109, class, event key); intervals are sorted first, so the order of the reports does not matter
method.median_interval_exact: distribution-free interval (x_(k), x_(n-k+1)) with the largest k such that P(Bin(n, 1/2) <= k-1) <= 0.025; median_exact_ci_coverage is its achieved coverage
method.unit: report: one case id of the faers pipeline (latest case version)
method.weibull: maximum likelihood with a half-day shift (same-day intervals are 0 days); 95 % likelihood-ratio interval of the shape; shape class early (interval below 1), random (contains 1) or wear_out (above 1). Cornelius 2012, Hatahira 2017, Hasegawa 2020

table.review_status: Methods reviewed by the statistician agent and class and event mappings by the pharmacologist agent (AI reviews, findings applied or listed as open items in .kiro/specs/faers-onset-table/); pending review by a pharmacist and a statistician.
